title: Finite free duality for nonempty ordered two-term tensors on one ringed site
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small category with Grothendieck topology $J$, $\mathcal O$ a commutative ring sheaf, $r\in\mathbf N$ and $b$ a family of $r+1$ global sections. The ordered negative two-term tensors $N_m=\bigotimes_i[\mathcal O\xrightarrow{b_i^{m+1}}\mathcal O]$ in degrees $-1,0$ of [def-cbc-signed-koszul-completion-model] have chain isomorphisms to $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P_m,\mathcal O[0])$, with $P_m$ the ordered positive two-term tensor of [def-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-system]. These intertwine the explicit negative transitions of [def-weil-pbc-ringed-negative-koszul-transitions] with the dual positive transitions. The empty-subset negative basis inclusion followed by the degree-zero isomorphism equals the degree-zero dual augmentation of [def-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-system], preceded by the inverse single-complex identification. This has no scheme, coefficient extension or exterior algebra. The empty-list case is proved separately in [def-weil-pbc-ringed-negative-koszul-transitions].

source.place: Tag 0A0E, lemma-derived-completion-koszul, the finite free negative Koszul complex and its dual identification; Modules on Sites Tags 03D8, 03EK and 0GMW for coefficient realization.

proof.text: Induct on the number of generators, proving the same normalized duality assertion for all lists, including the empty one. For length zero apply ringedNegativeKoszulZeroDuality, already proved in the transition module.

At a successor, use the tail isomorphism e_m from induction. Tensor it with the first negative factor, then apply the one-factor tensor-Hom isomorphism with K equal to the tail positive complex. The result has exactly the recursively defined negative source and Hom of the positive successor tensor as target.

For the transition square, first use the tail transition equation under the tensor functor. Move the first negative transition past the tensor of e_(m+1) by bifunctor naturality. Apply contravariant naturality of the one-factor comparison to the tail positive transition, followed by its first-factor transition equation. Contravariant functoriality combines the resulting maps into the successor positive transition; bifunctor naturality identifies its two orders.

Unfold only the successor empty-subset basis. The subset preimage is empty and both factor degrees are zero. Naturality of the total-tensor (0,0) inclusion moves the tensor of the tail isomorphism onto that tail basis. Replace the composite by the induction unit equation. The one-factor normalized projection equation, with p the tail projection, gives the desired successor dual unit because the positive projection is defined recursively by exactly that tensor of projections and U tensor U -> U.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0A0E; A3 formalizes induction using the normalized single-factor comparison, proving all recursive transition and empty-subset unit glue in Lean.

lean.statement:
theorem ringedNegativeKoszulSuccDuality
    {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
    (O : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}) (r : ℕ)
    (b : Fin (r + 1) → (O.obj ⋙ forget CommRingCat).sections) :
    ∃ e : ∀ m : ℕ, ringedNegativeKoszul O (r + 1) b m ≅
        (ringedKoszulDualTower O (r + 1) b).obj (op m),
      (∀ m, ringedNegativeKoszulTransition O (r + 1) b m ≫ (e m).hom =
        (e (m + 1)).hom ≫ (ringedKoszulDualTower O (r + 1) b).map
          (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ m)).op) ∧
      (∀ m, ringedNegativeKoszulBasis O (r + 1) b m ∅ 0 ≫ (e m).hom.f 0 =
        (HomologicalComplex.singleObjXSelf (.up ℤ) 0 _).inv ≫
          (ringedKoszulDualUnit O (r + 1) b m).f 0)
